A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LD-RPS study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete supplementary material support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-restoration experiments, recurrence and text-guidance ablations, and supplementary results across three random seeds.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and supplementary results, with several revised qualitative output examples.

M1.justification: The MLLM semantic guidance, F-PAM architecture and losses, two-stage posterior sampling, recurrent refinement and supplementary thresholding procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 retains the same operations.

E1.justification: Both retain LOLv1/LOLv2 enhancement, HSTS/RESIDE dehazing, Kodak24 denoising, and colorization and mixed-degradation demonstrations. Replacement illustration images remain within the existing task and domain coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 2–4 retain the same task-specific and unified comparator sets and applicability exclusions. The revised colorization comparison in Figure 7 still compares GDP with LD-RPS.

E3.justification: Reported evaluation settings, including 256×256 center crops and sampling schedules, are unchanged. Section 5.1 removes the sentence listing PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, PI and NIQE, but the same task-specific metric sets remain in the tables.

E4.justification: The recurrence and text-guidance ablations in Tables 5–6 and Figure 8, and the F-PAM and intermediate-generation analyses in Figures 10–11, are unchanged. The replaced illustrations introduce no new diagnostic or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Both report averaging over three seeds and retain the individual results for seeds 10, 20 and 123 in supplementary Tables 7–8. No uncertainty-reporting or statistical-estimation procedure changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 2–8 are unchanged. Figure 7 replaces the hikers example with a fish example in the joint colorization/denoising comparison. Figure 9 replaces the snake input/output and prompt with a rider/cattle example and changes the displayed penguin restoration.

T1.justification: Equations 1–15 retain the same mathematical content, including the posterior-sampling derivation and dynamic-thresholding equations. Changes in spacing and page placement introduce no new definitions, assumptions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about dataset-free, task-blind zero-shot restoration, semantic guidance, F-PAM, recurrent refinement and comparative superiority.

C2.justification: Interpretations of task-dependent recurrence, text-guidance benefits, pretrained-model hallucinations and baseline applicability remain unchanged. The revised qualitative examples are not accompanied by new explanations or limitations.

D1.justification: The Stable Diffusion/DDIM implementation, H20 hardware, parameter-selection description, sampling and threshold settings, and promised code/data access remain unchanged. Supplementary implementation details are retained under renumbered sections.

R1.justification: v3 adds USP and Flux-Text to diffusion background citations and Transplat to the introduction. It removes the four works previously cited alongside SSIM, LPIPS, PI and NIQE. Positioning relative to the core restoration and posterior-sampling methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 expands author contact information, adds an acknowledgements section, slightly shortens the introduction and removes the metric-list sentence. Supplementary sections are renumbered, while most prose and the narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 7 and 9 contain revised panels, and Figure 9 changes from pink/red styling to blue with adjusted spacing. Equation spacing and page flow also change, while the overall figure organization and table structures remain intact.

improvement.justification: The scientific argument and its supporting evidence are essentially preserved: the method, numerical tables, ablations and implementation disclosures are unchanged. Figure substitutions, added background citations and acknowledgements mainly update presentation; removing metric citations slightly reduces attribution. These limited edits do not materially change the paper’s overall quality.
